name: Anchored Facet Cubes Reconstruct Ample Families by One Cardinality Test
statement: Let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty antichain in $2^E$, let $\Sigma$ be its downward closure, choose an affine cube $C_T\subseteq Q_E$ with support $T$ for each $T\in\mathcal F$, and put $H=\bigcup_T C_T$. Then $H$ is ample with shattered complex $\Sigma$ exactly when $|H|=|\Sigma|$. In that case the selected cubes are precisely the maximal cubes of $H$, and $H$ is cornerless exactly when no vertex belongs to exactly one selected cube.
proof: The selected cubes strongly shatter every face of $\Sigma$, so the cardinality equality forces equality throughout the Sandwich inequalities and hence ampleness with the desired shadow. Conversely ampleness gives the equality. The carrier of a facet support has only the empty shattered face and therefore one placement, while the carrier of a nonfacet support is a nontrivial connected ample family, so every such cube extends. Thus exactly the selected facet cubes are maximal, and their incidence multiplicities give the corner test.
